title: Drum teachers: Roy Knapp, Art Layfield and Paul Ash
summary: Bertrand lists his teachers, including Roy Knapp and Art Layfield, formerly with Paul Ash. The interviewer says Layfield taught him too and they discuss the Oriental and McVickers theaters.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: I took lessons from the best musicians in this country. You know what I mean? I know.
People told me you were a really finished drummer.

I mean you knew all of the instruments. Me and Mr. Cusick, me and Mr. Roy Knapp, if you say that, let Mr. Roy Knapp say something about it. He was the man from the, what do you call it, the Minneapolis Symphony.
Oh yes, I've heard of him. And Roy's downtown now, he's taking care of everybody. He has a drum book out, I think.
And he, that's Roy, that's my buddy. And another fellow, let me get them together now, uh, got dog my tootin' time, Art Layfield. Oh yes. Used to be with Paul Ash. Mm-hmm.

That was my tutor too. You remember Paul Ash? Yes, I used to hear him at the theater down there. Oriental was one of those theaters. Well he was at the Oriental and the McVickers. The McVickers, that's where I had him. Yeah. I used to take Lesman Wren. Then I got bigger than him.
